 SF Chronicle Updated Thu, November 19, 2026 at 7:40 AM UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. The epicenter of Wednesday's quake near Central California. (SF Chronicle/Mapbox) An earthquake of preliminary magnitude 3.5 hit Tulare County on Wednesday night.
 The United States Geological Survey detected the quake at 10:40 p.m. with an epicenter 32.8 miles northeast of central Porterville and a depth of 3.0 miles.
 The fault that caused the quake was not immediately known, but the epicenter was on or near Kern Canyon fault zone, according to the USGS fault database. Explore the major California faults on our map.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In general, there is always a chance that any minor earthquake is a foreshock to a larger quake, but the risk is very low, in the single digits percentage-wise.
 Over the last seven days, there have been no other earthquakes above magnitude 3.0 within 100 miles of this area.
